card.name: Word before a medical term in warnings
card.fires_on: Responds to the word or word part just before a hyphenated or compound medical term in warnings. Typical cases are 'DNA' before '-damaging agents' and 'pulmonary' before 'fibrosis'.

modes.label: DNA before damaging
modes.description: The word DNA right after 'other' or 'with' in text about DNA-damaging agents and secondary leukemia.
modes.example: had received previous chemotherapy with platinum agents and/or other<< DNA>>-damaging agents, including radiotherapy

modes.label: Partway through a medical term
modes.description: A piece of a longer clinical term such as pulmonary, PML or Hand-Foot, where the rest of the term follows.
modes.example: Discontinue tretinoin capsules if the t(15;17) translocation or P<<ML>>/RARα fusion has not been identified

modes.label: Linking word before a regimen
modes.description: A word like 'plus' joining a drug name to a regimen name.
modes.example: in patients receiving POLIVY<< plus>> R-CHP.

card.plain: It fires on a word that is about to be followed by the rest of a medical term, mostly in warnings about side effects.
